thread:
support-jen: Customer acme-inc reported sudden throughput drop on their Dedicated pool (d-pool-12) ~0900 UTC. They see higher p99 latency and a rise in 429s. Can someone triage?

jamal: On it. any correlation with deploys or autoscale events?

support-jen: Customer says no deploys client-side, but we did an autoscale resize for that pool at 0855 where we returned a node and scaled down by 1.

mike: pulling metrics now — Grafana shows CPU on the GPUs fine, but average batch size dropped from ~7 tokens/request to ~1.8 around 0856. That would blow throughput.

sara: interesting. could be continuous-batcher window shrink or max_batch_tokens mismatch. Did model variant swap around the same time?

dinesh: checking model routing. At 0854 the routing service marked model `rwd-llama-3-quant` as preferred for that customer because of cost fallback. quant variant has smaller default max_batch_tokens = 256 vs 2048 for main model.

jamal: that explains per-batch token cap. small token cap -> lots of tiny micro-batches -> solver overhead -> throughput drop. need repro and mitigations.

ops-bot: autoscale event logged: pool=d-pool-12 action=scale_down delta=-1 time=2026-03-17T08:55:12Z autoscaler=v2

mike: can we confirm batcher config after variant swap? fetch batcher stats from a node: `curl -s http://10.2.12.45:8080/debug/batcher/stats | jq .`

jamal: pasted output from node: ```{"continuous_window_ms":10,"max_batch_tokens":256,"observed_avg_tokens_per_request":4.3,"observed_avg_requests_per_batch":1.9,"batch_rate_per_s":420}```

support-jen: copy of customer logs: `429 rate limited: token_over_budget` appears after 0856 and client retries pile up.

sara: hypothesis: routing promoted quant variant (lower max_batch_tokens) after node removal changed capacity plan; continuous batcher adapted windowing and with token ceiling low it started emitting tiny batches. Not noisy neighbor.

dinesh: I ran a quick simulated load against the pool with curl loop. Repro steps: 
1) `for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-3-quant","input":"short prompt"}' & done`
2) watch `/debug/batcher/metrics` on a node. Observed avg requests/batch ~2 and token-per-batch ~512 (because token cap 256 * 2). Throughput half of baseline.

mike: mitigation options: 
- immediate: pin customer routing to non-quant variant for pool d-pool-12 (fast rollback)
- short-term: bump per-pool batcher config max_batch_tokens override to 2048 to preserve packing behavior regardless of variant
- long-term: ensure routing decisions consider effective batch_token ceilings (add gating)

jamal: new action items: 
- Dinesh: pin routing (done?)
- Mike: push temporary max_batch_tokens override as service annotation to pool
- Sara: add regression alert for avg_requests_per_batch drop >40% after routing changes

ops-bot: routing-change: route_override applied pool=d-pool-12 model=rwd-llama-3-stable by dinesh at 09:12:03 UTC

dinesh: pinned to stable variant. early signs: avg_requests_per_batch climbing back to ~6, batch_rate down a bit but per-token throughput up.

support-jen: updated customer: rollback in progress, will monitor. they report lower latency already. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-oncall: follow-ups for RFC: 1) autoscaler should not remove nodes if routing topology would force a cheaper-but-smaller-token-cap model onto a pool (policy mismatch). 2) batcher should expose per-pool override and be part of rollout playbook. 3) add canary for variant swaps to measure packing impact.

mike: I've pushed the override for pool d-pool-12 and added a short-lived dashboard showing avg_requests_per_batch and max_batch_tokens per pool. Will follow up with a PR for the gating rule.

sara: thanks all. I'll create a postmortem note with root cause = routing/model-variant swap + autoscale timing -> effective max_batch_tokens regression leading to tiny batches. Recommend we treat this as a reliability bug and prioritize.

support-jen: marking customer ticket #CS-4721 as "monitoring". If numbers hold after 30m we'll close.

jamal: thumbs. good triage.

mike: one more note for reproducibility: if you want to replicate locally use this helper: ```bash
# simulate many short requests
for i in $(seq 1 800); do 
  curl -s -X POST http://10.2.12.45:8080/infer -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-3-quant","input":"hi"}' &
done
# then watch
watch -n1 curl -s http://10.2.12.45:8080/debug/batcher/stats | jq .
```

eng-runtime-oncall: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open until metrics stable.
